# `rewrite` dialect

CEIR-27 sec-72 the rewrite dialect: an AUTHORABLE declarative REWRITE-RULE program. A rewrite module is a SEPARATE asset (NOT the payload) whose rules a runtime driver (greedy_rewrite_rules, passes/rewrite_rules.hpp) applies to a payload -- so a plugin dialect ships a canonicalization/peephole WITHOUT editing the central C++ pattern array (canonicalize.hpp's kCanonPatterns, whose header notes it has NO plugin boundary; sec-72's DSL is exactly that boundary). A rule matches an op of a named ROOT kind under a CONSTRAINT and applies an ACTION. The TWO authored rules that express canonicalize.hpp's COMPLETE tensor.reshape set: 27c identity_reshape (a no-op reshape -> its input, RAUW-to-operand) + 27d reshape_of_reshape (reshape(reshape(x)) -> reshape(x), BUILD a new op over the grandchild operand). Vocabularies are CLOSED (enforced by find_rewrite_misuse, the find_resource/quant/transform_misuse house pattern) and grow by one entry when a new rule needs them (27d added the `operand_defined_by_root` constraint + `build_op_from_inner_operand` action). A rewrite.rule carries NO results/operands and NO effects (compile-time rule metadata, not runtime work) and is NOT Pure -- a rule is not a value computation, so Pure/CSE/DCE reasoning does not apply. ⛔ the re-match guard is UNIVERSAL (the DRIVER's contract, NOT a rule attr): BOTH actions RAUW result(result_idx) and LEAVE the dead op for DCE, so match REQUIRES result(result_idx) to still HAVE uses -- else re-firing on an already-rewritten op never terminates. Putting it in the driver means no rule author can forget it. ⛔ an action that WALKS a path (build_op_from_inner_operand) may only pair with the constraint that VALIDATES that path (operand_defined_by_root) -- find_rewrite_misuse rejects the cross-pairing (ActionNeedsConstraint), else a vocab-valid asset would deref a null/absent inner operand.

## `rewrite.rule`

One declarative rewrite rule: match op-kind `root` under `constraint`, apply `action` at result/operand indices.

One authored declarative rewrite rule. Match an op of kind `root` (an op-name compared via ctx.op_name) under `constraint`, apply `action` at the `result`/`operand` indices. constraint/action are CLOSED vocabularies enforced by find_rewrite_misuse (UnknownConstraint/UnknownAction); an index exceeding the MATCHED op's arity is a RUNTIME reject in greedy_rewrite_rules (arity is per-matched-op). NO results/operands/effects and NOT Pure -- rule metadata, not a value computation. The identity_reshape rule (this slice) is root=tensor.reshape, constraint=result_type_eq_operand, action=replace_result_with_operand, result=0, operand=0.
